subject: Demolition Delay for 56 Wareham Street
overview: The Medford Historical Commission found 56 Wareham Street to be preferably preserved, imposing an 18-month demolition delay. The commission also recommended two properties for National Register eligibility review and discussed commemorative design concepts for Thomas Brooks Park.

items.title: 56 Wareham Street preferably preserved hearing
items.summary: Following extensive public comment from neighbors opposing demolition, the commission voted that the property is preferably preserved, instituting an 18-month demolition delay.

items.title: Demolition applications and tabled hearings
items.summary: Hearings for 69 Court Street and 314 Winthrop Street were tabled, and the commission voted to accept the demolition application for 43 Allston Street.

items.title: National Register eligibility recommendations
items.summary: The commission voted to recommend both Shiloh Baptist Church and the historic buildings at Oak Grove Cemetery to the Massachusetts Historical Commission for determinations of National Register eligibility.

items.title: Thomas Brooks Park archeological cap
items.summary: Ryan shared design ideas and precedents from Portsmouth and Charlestown for an archaeological cap, pathways, and interpretive signage memorializing the house site and Pompeii's wall.

items.title: 2024 meeting schedule and administrative business
items.summary: The commission agreed on its 2024 meeting dates, decided to remain fully remote through June before reevaluating hybrid meetings, and tabled the slate of officers to January.

items.title: Updates on historical sites and ongoing business
items.summary: Commissioners discussed proposed archaeological testing at the Cross Street Cemetery commuter rail lot, CPA funding expectations, and canopy reconstruction progress at the former Medford cinema.

items.title: Meeting minutes
items.summary: The commission approved the meeting minutes from November 2023.
